newsitem.title: USA: Third L.A. high school athlete dies in accident.
newsitem.headline: Third L.A. high school athlete dies in accident.

text.p: The third Los Angeles area high school athlete to die in a freak accident in two weeks was taken off a life-support system Monday after his organs were removed for donation, officials said.
Kriston Palomo, 16, was fatally injured during a school baseball game Saturday when his larynx was crushed by the bill of a base runner's batting helmet as he tried to catch a fly ball.

A spokesman for St. Bernard's Roman Catholic School said Palomo was the star of the school's baseball team. He was honoured at a school memorial service Monday, after which the team decided it would continue to play for the rest of the season because that was what Palomo would have wanted.

Surgery to remove Palomo's liver, corneas, and heart valves was carried out Sunday and he was removed from the life-support system early Monday. His parents had requested that he be kept on the system so his organs could be removed for donation, a hospital spokeswoman said.
On April 29, Heath Taylor, 17, a member of the William S. Hart High School track and field team, died after a pole vaulting accident when he bounced off the landing pad and hit the ground head first.
On April 22, Craig Kelford, 16, of Peninsula High School, died after being struck in the back of the head by a discus thrown by another athlete.
